title: On the Born rule in a new quantum approach
abstract: In the context of a new approach towards quantum foundation, the Born rule is proved under a weak condition through several steps. The sole weak condition behind the Born rule is called the transition probability principle, which is closely related to the likelihood principle of statistics. This condition is discussed from several points of view. The whole approach leads to a simpler state concept than the traditional one in finite-dimensional quantum mechanics.
summary: This paper proposes a new quantum foundation approach to derive the Born rule. It achieves this by introducing the 'transition probability principle' as a weak, necessary condition. The framework develops a simpler state concept than traditional quantum mechanics, showing how this principle forces the quantum probability rules to take their standard form.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive the Born rule within a novel quantum foundation approach, seeking to establish it under minimal, weak physical assumptions.
main_result: The Born rule, $P(V = c_k|U = b_j) = v(V, c_k)^\dagger v(U, b_j)$, is derived by assuming the 'transition probability principle,' which relates conditional probabilities to likelihood effects.
method: The derivation uses a framework of 'theoretical variables' and 'accessible variables,' connecting generalized probability measures derived from likelihood effects to standard quantum mechanical expectation values via Busch's theorem.
model_or_system: The model is abstract, dealing with mathematical structures like 'theoretical variables' and 'complementary variables' (analogous to position and momentum). It aims to provide a state concept simpler than traditional finite-dimensional quantum mechanics.
key_observables: Conditional probabilities $P(V|U)$, likelihood effects $F$, and the density operator $\sigma$.
important_parameters: The structure relies on the existence of complementary variables and the assumption of a transition probability principle.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the 'transition probability principle,' a weak condition related to the likelihood principle of statistics, which is proposed to be sufficient to prove the Born rule.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining theoretical variables and complementary variables (Theorem 1a/1b) to establishing state representation and conditional probability formulas. It then uses the transition probability principle to prove that the likelihood measure must be a standard quantum probability measure, culminating in the derivation of the Born rule (Theorem 4).
why_interesting: This work tackles one of the most fundamental open problems in quantum foundations—the derivation of the Born rule—using a novel mathematical framework that might simplify the understanding of quantum state concepts.
